title: How to Levitate
summary: This instructional video catalogs several levitation illusions, ranging from inexpensive, home-friendly tricks to more elaborate stage effects. It starts with a simple blanket-illusion that uses linked shoes and a cover to hide foot movements, then details a pants-slit method that disguises a hidden leg movement with Velcro-tied footwear, followed by a floor-based stage illusion that relies on a concealed vertical support and floor coverings to hide the rigging, and concludes with a hoop-and-beam routine designed for visibility from multiple angles. Each method is described with required props, setup notes, and the basic illusion mechanism as presented by the presenter.
topics: floor coverings to disguise rigging (sand, blanket, rug)
hoop levitation around a hidden beam
angles and visibility considerations in levitation effects

sections.title: Simple at-home blanket-illusion with linked shoes
sections.description: Describes a method where two shoes are linked so that moving one causes the other to move. The performer covers themselves with a blanket; under cover, the right foot is moved from one shoe to the other, while the left foot is lifted, creating the appearance of levitation when the blanket is removed and the shoes appear to be hovering.

sections.title: Pants-slit levitation using jeans and hidden-foot mechanics
sections.description: Outlines a low-cost method: cut a slit from top to bottom on the right leg of baggy jeans, glue or tape the pant to the bottom of the shoe, and use velcro to keep the shoes together so one foot can be freed and pulled out of the slit. The right foot steps onto a stool while the back of the legs remain connected, creating the illusion of floating as the body rises.

sections.title: Floor-based stage levitation with concealed support (popular stage method)
sections.description: Introduces a widely used stage illusion where a floor covering (blanket, sand, or rug) hides a steel support that runs from the floor up a staff and down the performer's back, forming a hidden seat. The audience cannot see the beam, enabling the illusion of levitation as the performer appears to rise with the support hidden on the floor and body.

sections.title: Hoop levitation around a hidden vertical beam
sections.description: Describes a hoop maneuver where the hoop moves over the body from one end to the other, avoiding the visible beam. From the front it appears the hoop traverses the entire body, but it strategically covers the concealed support, enabling a convincing levitation illusion.
